about: Word timings for a voice that doesn't report them (Supertonic), estimated from the text and the audio. Input: the text, and audio described as a list of stretches, each sound (a steady tone) or silence, at `sampleRate`. Output: one timing per whitespace-separated word, in order; only the words listed in `expected` are checked, each start and end within `tolerance` seconds. Pauses in the audio are matched to punctuation in the text, in order; words between them share the sound by their length.

cases.name: leading and trailing silence aren't given to any word
cases.text: Mr. Bennet replied that he had not.

cases.name: each pause is pinned to the comma or semicolon it falls nearest
cases.text: It is a truth universally acknowledged, that a single man in possession of a good fortune, must be in want of a wife.

cases.name: a comma said without a pause leaves the words spread evenly by length
a pause with no punctuation near it doesn't move the words around it
cases.text: The boatman was asleep and the water was black and still.
